title: Remove a staple without tearing the papers
instruction: Remove the staple without tearing the papers, then lay the two sheets separately.
context: Preparing documents for scanning requires releasing a clinched fastener while preserving thin paper around its holes.
setup: Proposed fixed setup in setup.json: two aligned white 80 gsm paper sheets, each 210 × 148 × 0.1 mm, centred at x=0.32 m, y=0 on the 747.5 mm station table. One steel staple has a 12.8 mm crown, 6 mm legs and 0.50 × 0.30 mm wire section, clinched 12 mm inside both nearest sheet edges. A 55 × 35 × 25 mm spring-open steel-jaw/ABS staple remover lies at x=0.28 m, y=-0.20 m. Exact nominal dimensions/placements are fixed; physical match and setup screenshot are unvalidated. Reset spawns the stapled stack 0.5 mm above the tabletop so the clinch does not intersect it, then lets the thin sheets settle and drape naturally before policy control; no hidden pins or rigid-paper substitute.
scoring: 0.5 when at least one staple leg is entirely clear of both sheets. 1.0 when both legs are clear and the sheets lie separately with at least 30 mm between their nearest edges, released for three seconds. Any tear extending over 2 mm beyond an original hole, new damage elsewhere, broken staple, altered sheets or invalid evidence gives zero. All other outcomes score zero.
run_limit: Proposed 2,400 control steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz); no robot run yet.
reset_notes: Use fresh matched paper and one fresh staple for every trial. Record both sides before and after. Reuse the remover only while intact.
fidelity: CPU steel-plasticity, paper-fracture and one-leg jaw-contact probes exist, with uncalibrated parameters. The native PhysX plastic-hinge hook is untested. A complete deformable paper, puncture-hole, staple-extraction and robot scene is not implemented.
scores: Not run. No demo, Dream score or media exists. This is not submission metadata.
